subject: harvester ant
title: This Ant Queen Gives Birth to Sons of a Different Species

scenes.text: This ant queen gives birth to another species.
Her nest holds two kinds of sons. Hairy ones like her, and hairless ones from a different species.
Those two species split apart over five million years ago.
Why? Her workers are all hybrids, which takes sperm from that other species.
So she grows its males from her own eggs, using stored sperm.
She doesn't need the other species nearby anymore. She keeps a copy of it at home.

description:
Queens of the Iberian harvester ant lay eggs that hatch into males of a different species, Messor structor, cloned from stored sperm.
All of their workers are hybrids that need structor fathers, so the queens keep a home-grown line of the other species, a first known in any animal.
What would you call this: parenting or farming?
first_comment: Scientists call it xenoparity, birth of a foreign species. The two species are as genetically different as animals that split over five million years ago. Can you think of anything weirder?
